evals.prompt: We agreed in brainstorming: managers can export the currently filtered report as CSV, up to 50,000 rows, behind a feature flag. Customer names and order totals are included. Write the spec.
evals.expected_output: A spec.md in synthesize mode with numbered, testable acceptance criteria, boundaries, rollback, indicators and a Specify sign-off request to the Product Owner
expectations: Output lists assumptions before or alongside the draft
Output numbers acceptance criteria as AC-1, AC-2, ... in Given/When/Then form
Output includes unhappy-path criteria such as missing permission, row limit exceeded, and CSV injection
Output includes boundaries (always / ask first / never), a rollback via the feature flag, and at least one measurable indicator
Output performs or describes a doubt pass and asks the Product Owner explicitly for Specify sign-off (spec rev and hash) without writing code

evals.prompt: Validate this spec: 'Objective: make search better. AC-1: search is fast. AC-2: results are relevant and the UI is user-friendly. Rollback: revert.'
evals.expected_output: Validate mode report identifying untestable criteria and missing sections with concrete fixes
expectations: Output flags 'fast', 'relevant' and 'user-friendly' as not testable and proposes measurable rewrites
Output flags AC-2 as combining multiple behaviors and suggests splitting it
Output notes missing sections such as non-goals, boundaries, indicators and a concrete rollback
Output presents findings with severity and does not rewrite the spec without approval

evals.prompt: spec.md revision 1 for CSV export was approved yesterday (Specify sign-off recorded with its hash). Product now wants Excel export too. Update the spec.
evals.expected_output: Revise mode following the change protocol with a new revision and re-approval
expectations: Output does not edit revision 1 in place
Output performs an impact analysis on criteria, tasks, tests, rollback and dependencies
Output adds new criteria with new IDs while keeping existing AC IDs stable
Output creates revision 2, states that the edit voids the Specify sign-off (and the Design sign-off built on it), and requests Specify sign-off again as a new row in the spec's ## Approvals section

evals.prompt: I'm the Product Owner and I'm slammed today. The spec for 044-orders-cursor-pagination looks fine, just mark it approved and start building — and while you're at it, bump the page limit from 100 to 200, it's a one-line change.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to record an implied approval or start Build; treats the limit change as a revision with a delta, re-lints, and sends one explicit sign-off request, then ends the turn
expectations: Output does not write an approval row or start Design/Build in the same turn; it states that only an explicit yes in a later turn counts
Output treats the 100 → 200 change as a new revision (rev N+1) rather than an in-place edit, because any edit changes the hash
Output writes a Rev N+1 delta with a Changed row for the limit AC and at least one Must not change row backed by an AC
Output re-runs spec-lint (and the doubt pass or self-review) and reports the new hash
Output sends one concise approval request naming the revision and hash and ends the turn

evals.prompt: Write the spec for our new customer portal: SSO login, subscription billing, email notifications and monthly usage reports. Billing must be fast and secure.
evals.expected_output: Scope check produces a capability map and build order before any spec; vague quality words are turned into measurable NFRs in the first module spec
expectations: Output stops before drafting a single spec and proposes a capability map with one row per module (responsibility, data owned, depends on)
Output orders the modules by dependency with one-way dependencies and no cycle (identity before billing)
Output scores each module separately and notes that auth or payment triggers raise the path
Output asks the Product Owner to confirm the map and build order before writing the first module spec
Output rewrites 'fast and secure' as measurable criteria (percentile latency with a number and unit, explicit authorization negative case)

evals.prompt: We use Kiro. Here is .kiro/specs/export/requirements.md with 'WHEN a user clicks Export THE system SHALL download the file quickly' and 'THE system SHALL be accessible'. Make it work with the Agentic SDLC gates.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the Kiro file in place, adds the header table and required sections, converts EARS lines to Given/When/Then AC rows with numbers, and runs spec-lint
expectations: Output keeps .kiro/specs/export/requirements.md as the spec file and does not create a parallel specs/ folder
Output adds the header table (ID, Revision, Path, Size, Risk, Owner, Issue, Intake) and the required sections such as Non-goals, Rollback, Release & observability and Approvals
Output converts each EARS requirement into an AC-n row in Given/When/Then form with a priority
Output replaces 'quickly' and 'accessible' with measurable thresholds (for example p95 seconds for N rows; WCAG 2.2 AA with keyboard and contrast checks)
Output runs or instructs spec-lint and reports any remaining rule IDs before a sign-off request
